components.css: .ds-plate{margin:0;position:relative;color:var(--ink, #1b347f);font-family:'Archivo', 'Arial Narrow', system-ui, sans-serif}.ds-dim{position:relative;height:22px;margin:0 0 6px;font:500 11px/1 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace;color:var(--ink-3, #5a6ca3)}.ds-dim::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:11px;border-top:1px solid var(--line-strong, rgba(27,52,127,.55))}.ds-dim::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:5px;height:12px;border-left:1px solid var(--line-strong, rgba(27,52,127,.55));border-right:1px solid var(--line-strong, rgba(27,52,127,.55))}.ds-dim span{position:relative;z-index:1;display:table;margin:0 auto;padding:0 8px;background:var(--field, #f3f6fb)}.ds-frame{position:relative;border:1px solid var(--line-strong, rgba(27,52,127,.55));padding:8px;background:var(--sheet, #f8fafd);box-shadow:var(--plate-shadow, 0 1px 0 rgba(27,52,127,.25),0 18px 40px -22px rgba(27,52,127,.45))}.ds-img{aspect-ratio:16/9;background:linear-gradient(135deg,var(--ink-3, #5a6ca3),var(--ink, #1b347f))}.ds-tag{position:absolute;left:35%;top:30%;transform:translate(-50%,-50%);width:24px;height:24px;border-radius:50%;display:grid;place-items:center;background:var(--sheet, #f8fafd);color:var(--red, #c4321a);border:1.5px solid var(--red, #c4321a);font:700 11px/1 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace;box-shadow:0 2px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,.35);cursor:pointer;transition:transform .3s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1),background-color .2s}.ds-tag:hover{background:var(--red, #c4321a);color:var(--sheet, #f8fafd);transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(1.18)}.ds-plate figcaption{margin-top:10px;font-size:13px;color:var(--ink-3, #5a6ca3)}

narrative.overview:
The site is a set of construction drawings. A JSON spec is the drawing; the file it builds is the plate mounted beside it. Every page is a sheet with a drawing border and a sheet number, artifacts sit in dimensioned frames, and numbered tags tie a spec line to the part of the output it built. The aim is that a visitor reads "spec in, file out" at a glance and trusts it because the page looks like something that gets checked, not marketed.

Two materials carry the world. Dark is cyanotype: white linework on Prussian blue. Light is whiteprint: diazo blue linework on near-white. Both draw on a 24px graph grid. Redline, the markup colour of a reviewed drawing, is the only accent: leader lines, revision marks, sheet numbers, focus rings, hover underlines. The whole system is hairlines and type. There are no fills, no cards with radius, no gradients except the graph grid.

The build refuses the dark neon bento grid and the cream editorial page that developer tools default to. That rejection is the one confirmed visual anti-reference (direction contract, seed 149445c2). Voice stays minimal, in line with PRODUCT.md: few words, the artifact shown instead of described.
keyCharacteristics: Linework first: 1px hairlines in ink at 24% and 55% alpha do the work that fills and shadows do elsewhere.
Square corners everywhere; the only circles are detail tags, as on a real drawing.
Archivo at condensed width in heavy caps for lettering; JetBrains Mono for every measurement, spec and sheet number.
One accent (redline), used only for markup and state.
Every figure carries a mono caption ("Plate 01", a dimension line) that states something checkable.
Light and dark are co-equal themes, switchable (auto, light, dark), both held to AA contrast.

rules.name: The Redline Rule
rules.body: Redline marks; it does not decorate. It appears as a line, a number, a ring, a small tag or a hover state. Large surfaces and text blocks are never redline.

rules.name: The Two Materials Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are the same drawing on different stock. Every colour is a token with a light and a dark value; no component hard-codes a hue that exists in only one theme.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px lines (--rule). The 2px border is reserved for one object, the install stamp, because it is the document the visitor must act on.

rules.name: The Lettering Rule
rules.body: Condensed width and heavy weight are for lettering only: titles, sheet names, labels. Anything a visitor reads as a sentence is Archivo at width 100%.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: A measurement used as a label or data cell, a file name, a command, a sheet number or a line of spec is JetBrains Mono. Numbers inside a sentence or a bold item title stay in the reading face.

rules.name: The Case Follows Meaning Rule
rules.body: Page titles and group lettering are uppercase; skill and command names are lowercase because that is how they are typed.

rules.name: The Mounted Plate Rule
rules.body: Only the artifact is lifted. Text panels, spec panels, stamps and title blocks stay flat and bordered.

dos: Do draw structure with 1px hairlines (hairline, hairline-strong); keep the 2px border for the install stamp only.
Do keep every corner square. Circles are for detail tags only.
Do use redline only as a line, number, ring, tag or state: leader lines, sheet numbers, focus ring, hover underline.
Do set measurements, file names, commands, sheet numbers and spec lines in JetBrains Mono; set lettering in condensed heavy Archivo.
Do caption every figure with a plate number and a fact that can be checked in the code.
Do define every colour as a token with a light and a dark value, and check any new pairing for WCAG AA in both themes.
Do keep the focus ring as is: 2px redline, 3px offset, on every interactive element.
Do guard every motion (leader draw, scroll, hover lift, loop playback) with prefers-reduced-motion; transitions are 0.2 to 0.4s on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).
Do keep a plain-HTML fallback: the page must read without JavaScript; pa.js only adds theme, copy, scroll-spy, loop playback and leader lines.
donts: Don't make a dark neon bento grid or a cream editorial page. That is the confirmed anti-reference.
Don't fill large areas or text blocks with redline.
Don't put a soft shadow on text panels, spec panels or stamps. Lift the mounted artifact only.
Don't set body-length copy in condensed width, or set a measurement in Archivo.
Don't add rounded cards, pills or chips. The form language is frames, mats and rules.
Don't use imagery that is not a real output from the skills; thumbnails, clips and posters come from files in the repo, never mock-ups.
Don't introduce a second accent colour. Hue variety belongs inside the artifacts shown, not in the site chrome.
